answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with mutual-liability pools: agents join small groups that stake together into a shared fund, and if one member is caught faking, the whole pool is slashed. A falcon-eyed auditor samples members at random, so a farm cannot hide hollow identities inside an honest group, because the group vets every newcomer with its own money on the line. Trust grows like a vine through these vetted groups, and each fake cluster must fund a full pool of its own, making mass forgery pay full price per fake.
